title: If the Oil Ran Out: Imagined Situations

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si* + imperfect subjunctive from B1 Unit 4: *Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con el profesor*. You imagine a situation that is unlikely or contrary to fact, and the result goes in the conditional. Oil economies and rocket launches are full of "what would happen if" questions.

sections.title: If + imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional
rows: Si el petróleo se acabara, la economía de Guyana tendría que cambiar.
if the oil ran out, the economy would have to change
Si los cohetes salieran de Europa, necesitarían más combustible.
if the rockets left from Europe, they would need more fuel
Si no hubiera petróleo, Guyana dependería más del oro.
*hubiera* is the imperfect subjunctive of *haber*: if there were no oil
Si el centro espacial estuviera lejos del ecuador, gastaría más combustible.
*estuviera* from *estuvieron*: if the centre were far from the equator

items.spanish: Si el petróleo se acabara, la economía de Guyana tendría que cambiar.
items.english: If the oil ran out, the economy of Guyana would have to change.

items.spanish: Si el centro espacial estuviera en Europa, los cohetes gastarían más combustible.
items.english: If the space centre were in Europe, the rockets would use more fuel.

items.spanish: Si no hubiera petróleo, la economía de Guyana dependería más del azúcar, del arroz y del oro.
items.english: If there were no oil, the economy of Guyana would depend more on sugar, rice and gold.

items.spanish: Si Guyana tuviera más ingresos, podría construir más escuelas.
items.english: If Guyana had more income, it could build more schools.

sections.content: Never put the conditional after *si*: *si se acabara*, not *si se acabaría*. The verb after *si* agrees with its subject: *si el petróleo se acabara* (singular), *si los cohetes salieran* (plural). For things that are true or likely, use the real *si* clauses you know from B1 Unit 8 instead.
